paragraphs: Rabbi Abba son of Rav Yitzchak, Menachot 106a as cited by Hyman. See [Menachot 110a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.110a.4).[^4]
In [Yerushalmi Yevamot 12:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.12.1.11) he is called Rabbi Ba. Rav Ada son of Rav Yitzchak, [Yoma 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.17a.2).
Rav Acha son of Yitzchak, Shabbat ch. 3, halakhah 4.
Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav Yitzchak, [Avodah Zarah 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.33b.4).

Rav Chanan-Chinena-Chanina son of Yitzchak, [Yerushalmi Berakhot 6:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.6.1.9). Tuvia son of Yitzchak, [Eruvin 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.28b.21).

Rav Nachman son of Yitzchak, [Berakhot 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.5b.24). Rava son of Yitzchak, [Sotah 46b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.46b.14). Rabbah son of Yitzchak, [Yevamot 71b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.71b.14).
Rav Shila son of Yitzchak, the old Midrash Tehillim, chapter 91.
Rav Shmuel son of Rav Yitzchak, [Berakhot 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.31b.27).[^3]

notes.text: The heading and checked Yoma passage support Yitzchak in the abbreviated patronymic. “The old Midrash Tehillim” is retained as Hyman’s description without assigning a particular edition. This is a collective list.

The consulted Yoma 17a explicitly names Rav Ada son of Rav Yitzchak. The heading is a collective patronymic list, not proof that all the listed men shared one father. Hyman’s “old Midrash Tehillim” description is retained without assigning an independently uninspected exact edition.

The consulted Eruvin reads Rabbah bar Tuvia bar Yitzchak. In Berakhot 31b, the speaker is Rabbi Shmuel son of Rabbi Yitzchak, alongside Hyman’s Rav titles. The Yerushalmi passage about turnip gives Rabbi Chinena son of Yitzchak.
The linked passage names Rabbi Abba son of Rav Yitzchak speaking in Rav Chisda’s name. It also gives a separate version in which Rav Yehudah speaks in Rav’s name.
